method: At each change of support: gravity in the holder frame, the contacts that can push back, the open direction of escape, and the result with power removed. The tracked FUEL's path is now fitted to the free-piece trials in field-trials.json, which solve capture, entry, launch and delivery; this review still covers what those single-piece trials do not: power removed and loaded driving.

rows.support: Carpet in front of the bumper, under the belt module
rows.resisting: Carpet; the bottom pulley stands 20 mm into the top of a floor FUEL, so the belt takes it as the robot drives on
rows.disposition: accepted: no custody is claimed before the belt grips

rows.support: Vertical belt pinch against the bumper face
rows.resisting: Belt back run in front and bumper cover behind, 20 mm inside one FUEL diameter apart; the acquisition trial presses the FUEL 11.2 mm into the bumper and 11.0 mm into the belt
rows.powerOff: Drops back to the carpet outside the robot, the safe direction
rows.disposition: gate G4: the acquisition trial captures at 17.5 mm squeeze and fails at 15 mm; measure compression, cover friction and lift speed

rows.support: Top of the climb, under the top roller
rows.resisting: Top roller lowered 20 mm into the FUEL's path, belt in front, bumper behind
rows.escape: Back down the pinch if the roller stalls
rows.disposition: gate G4: the roller must carry the piece over the bumper's top edge

rows.resisting: Side walls to 715 mm, front lip to 170 mm, front upper wall from 482 mm, rear wall
rows.escape: Forward over the lip through the 312 mm throat under hard braking; over the walls if heaped above them
rows.disposition: gate G2: ten loaded 0.5 g stops with at most one FUEL lost; fallback is a passive throat flap

rows.support: Seat on the stopped floor belt against the stopped flywheel
rows.resisting: Flywheel above and behind (0.02 mm indentation at rest in the entry trial), belt below; nothing in front
rows.escape: Forward along the lane under braking; into the pinch if the belt runs toward the stopped wheel (3.2 to 5.9 mm in the entry trials)
rows.disposition: gate G7: no hold-back is designed; the belt backs the FUEL off before spin-up, which the launch trials need once the FUEL is at rest 0.44 mm or more into the wheel (0.23 mm launches without it; a penalty-contact threshold, not a measurement); loaded stops are gate G2

rows.resisting: Hood below and behind, flywheel above; the gap is the FUEL diameter less 12 mm
rows.powerOff: A FUEL in the wrap stays squeezed between the stopped wheel and the hood inside the robot
rows.disposition: restrained; launch trials pass from 8 to 16 mm squeeze and fail at 6 and 20 mm (gate G7)

rows.support: Hood wrap to release at the hood end, -149.5 deg about the wheel axis
rows.gravity: Along the hood toward the pinch
rows.escape: Released by design at the hood end

rows.support: Robot hanging on two hooks at 70 mm
rows.gravity: Robot pitches rear-down about the rung
rows.resisting: Jaws on the rung's far side and the front bumper on both uprights (about 634 N horizontal at 70.3 kg) across 23.9 mm of overlap per upright
rows.escape: A lateral offset beyond 23.9 mm loses one upright; the rung leaves the throat if the jaw does not reach below its equator
rows.powerOff: The winch must hold 690 N without power; the cable load peaks at 1043 N during the lift in the hang trial
rows.disposition: gate G3: test at 0 and +/-25 mm offset with the brake holding 1.5 x 690 N; add a spring latch under the rung if the jaw slips
